title: Sensor-error bounds permitted equal longest joint-exposure runs in September but not August in North Wales in 2021
abstract: We tested whether sensor-error bounds for total joint high-ozone and dry-air hours also preserve duration contrasts. We used 1,464 complete hourly records from August and September 2021 in a North Wales wildflower experiment. We proved sharp bounds for longest runs and hours in runs of at least six hours under flexible bounded errors. With errors up to 0.5 C, 5 humidity percentage points and 5 ppb ozone, longest-run lower contrasts were 5 and 3 hours in August, but zero at both tested high-ozone targets in September. Six-hour-run totals showed the same month difference. Total joint-hour lower contrasts stayed positive in all four comparisons. Twice the error limits permitted negative September duration contrasts, while August duration lower limits stayed positive. These are deterministic sensitivity bounds, not confidence intervals or measured errors. One dome per treatment, a shared ambient sensor, unknown source gap filling and one site-year limit inference. No flower response or causal climate effect was tested. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and independent numerical checks are included. The observations overlap prior campaign exposure studies; the duration test is new.

display.caption: Heated-minus-ambient duration contrasts. Dots use released readings. Lines are exact bounds under assumed errors up to 0.5 C, 5 humidity points and 5 ppb ozone. Both September bounds include zero. Bounds do not express sampling uncertainty.
